title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 19
paragraphs: When the Lacedaemonians reached the Isthmus, they encamped there; and when the rest of the Peloponnesians who favored the better cause heard this — and some, too, because they saw the Spartans going out — they did not think it right to lag behind. So from the Isthmus, when the sacrifices had proved favorable, they all marched together and came to Eleusis; and having performed sacrifices there too, with favorable signs they marched on, and the Athenians went with them, having crossed from Salamis and joined them at Eleusis. When they had come to Erythrai in Boeotia, they learned that the barbarians were encamped on the Asopos, and perceiving this they drew up against them on the lower slopes of Kithairon.
